fields.name: highlight_frame
fields.description: Write null when memory is empty and no cube highlight has appeared. If the carried value is null, inspect all motion frames and store the earliest frame clearly showing white circular areas beneath the highlighted cubes. Ignore the white square beneath the button. Once a label is stored, carry it unchanged even when the white areas disappear. e.g. "E17"
fields.annotation: Initially null. On the first cycle containing visible white circular areas beneath cubes, store the earliest frame in that cycle clearly showing the highlighted set. Retain that label thereafter, including after the highlights disappear. The white square supporting the button is not a cube highlight. e.g. "E17"

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Initialize false. Set true when this cycle shows the closed fingertips down in contact with the button following a pressing descent, including a contact-limited TCP height around z=0.024. Otherwise preserve the carried value. Highlights alone do not establish a press. e.g. false
fields.annotation: Initially false. Set true at the first cycle showing the closed fingertips down in contact with the button after the pressing descent; the observed TCP may stop around z=0.024 rather than reaching the commanded z=0.0075. Keep true thereafter. Do not set true merely because highlights appear. e.g. false

fields.name: completed_targets
fields.description: Initialize to "[]". From highlight_frame, number only the individually highlighted cubes by increasing original world y, then increasing original world x, starting at 1. These are stable identity labels, not pickup priorities; never renumber using positions changed by handling. Match a held cube to its highlighted identity using position, color, and this cycle's motion frames. Add its identifier when this cycle visibly shows it held off the table after a completed pickup lift with TCP approximately z=0.15, regardless of selection order. Serialize the identifiers in increasing numeric order with a comma and space between entries. Preserve membership through lowering, release, and retreat. Do not add identities for low grasps, commanded lifts, empty grasps, or an action executing no steps. An identity already present must not be added again when its cube remains held. e.g. "[1, 3]"
fields.annotation: Initially "[]". Assign stable identifiers to only the individually highlighted cubes in highlight_frame by increasing original world y, then increasing original world x, numbered starting at 1. This numbering identifies cubes and does not prescribe pickup order; never renumber using positions changed by handling. Store the identifiers of cubes whose completed pickup lifts have been observed, serialized as an ascending numeric list with a comma and space between entries. Add an identifier at the first cycle observing that cube held off the table after a pickup lift with TCP approximately z=0.15, regardless of which other targets have been completed. Do not add it at a low grasp or when a lift is merely commanded. Preserve membership through return, release, and retreat; never add an identifier twice. e.g. "[1, 3]"

action:
Start with an open hand and approach the button. Interpret all positions in world coordinates using the supplied camera calibration; estimate button and cube locations from their geometry, not raw image left/right. Back-project a visible surface center onto that surface's horizontal height plane, not automatically onto z=0. Estimate surface height and center from object geometry and both calibrated current views where available. For pixel p=(u,v,1), use the corresponding camera's calibration to compute world ray origin C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1 p. Intersect with the surface plane z=h using X=C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Use the current wrist camera's extrinsics for wrist pixels, not the front camera's extrinsics. For the button, localize the raised circular pressing surface rather than its white base. For a resting cube, localize the top-face center, not the center of the entire visible silhouette. For the approximately 4 cm cubes, use a top-face plane approximately 0.04 m above the tabletop, refining the height from visible cube geometry and calibrated views. Back-project the top-face center onto that plane using the appropriate camera calibration and refine with the current calibrated wrist view. Neither the tabletop plane nor the prescribed grasp TCP height is the cube's top-face plane. Use the resulting world x,y for object-centered approach and contact waypoints, retaining the separately specified TCP waypoint heights. Use the wrist view to refine alignment. Approximate hover alignment permits the next operation but does not make the achieved TCP x,y the object center. Recover target identities from highlight_frame after their white areas disappear, matching by position as well as color; never select every cube of a highlighted color. Use the observations of this cycle together with carried memory to recognize newly completed presses and lifts before selecting the action.

Button rules: If button_pressed is false and the hand is not yet above the button, move to its center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. At approximate button hover, allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm to proceed to the next operation, but do not treat the achieved TCP x,y as the button center. Before closing and again before pressing, estimate the button center from the current calibrated views, refining it with the wrist image. With open fingers at approximate hover, command that button-centered x,y at z=0.15 and close on arrival. With closed fingers at approximate hover and no observed contact yet, descend directly to the newly estimated button-centered x,y at z=0.0075 with fingers closed. Once contact is observed, retract to the button center at z=0.15, keeping closed; do not repeat the press merely because the actual contact height is higher than the command. After retracting, open at the button approach waypoint before traveling to a cube.

Pickup rules: Recover individually highlighted identities from highlight_frame using the same stable numbering as completed_targets. Robot-right is negative y and appears on the left of the front image. Match identities by position as well as color; numbering is not pickup priority. Exclude every identity in completed_targets, including any newly completed lift observed this cycle. If the open hand at hover is already aligned within roughly 1–1.5 cm above an uncompleted highlighted cube, select that cube and descend rather than redirecting to another target. Otherwise, when ready for lateral travel, select an uncompleted highlighted cube; absent an explicit goal ordering, any such target is eligible. Do not infer a color or spatial pickup priority from the identity numbering. With open fingers and adequate table clearance, approach its center at z=0.15. Use roll=3.1416 and pitch=0. Back-project two endpoints of a cube top-face edge onto the same top-face height plane using the calibrated ray-plane intersection. From their world-coordinate difference compute theta=atan2(delta_y,delta_x). Choose among theta+k*pi/2, for integer k, the square-equivalent edge-aligned yaw requiring the least angular rotation from the current hand yaw, accounting for angle wrapping. Do not negate theta based on image appearance or copy an image-plane edge angle. Preserve that alignment during descent and lift. Only when the open hand is approximately aligned above the selected uncompleted target, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm; if already aligned, descend rather than commanding another hover. An open hand at hover above a returned, completed cube must instead approach an uncompleted highlighted target at z=0.15 with fingers open. With the cube grasped at low height, lift vertically to z=0.15 with fingers closed, preserving the aligned yaw. Estimate its grasp center from the visible cube and wrist geometry rather than treating a small TCP tracking error as a new target location.

Handling additional targets: Once a pickup lift is visibly complete, include its identity in completed_targets even if the cube is subsequently returned. Recognize this completion before deciding whether any uncompleted highlighted target remains. If one remains and a completed cube is still held at hover height, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.01, retaining current orientation, and open on arrival. If the hand is low and open over that returned cube, retract vertically to approximately z=0.15 with fingers open before moving laterally. When retracted, approach an uncompleted highlighted target, not the cube just returned. When every highlighted identity is completed, keep the final lifted cube held; success should end the episode without requiring a placement.

For every gripper-only change, first construct the nominal object-centered waypoint rather than copying the achieved TCP pose. If that waypoint already provides at least 2 mm of translation from the reported TCP pose, do not add a nudge. Otherwise add a small upward adjustment within 5 mm so that the translation is at least 2 mm. Do not advance memory on an action that executed no steps. If alignment or grasp evidence is ambiguous, use the current wrist image to correct the relevant object-centered approach at safe height; a failed empty grasp should be retried without counting it. If no target evidence has yet been captured after the button operation, use a short bounded wait specifically to observe the highlight display and inspect every returned frame. Do not invent targets or repeatedly press a confirmed button. For an otherwise unmatched situation, preserve known task facts, keep a visibly held cube closed, and retract vertically to safe clearance before reassessing.
